rem:archimedean-chirality: Remark Chirality as Reeb orientation. The Reeb vector field \xi on the CR manifold M carries a natural orientation. The sign of the contact form \varTheta(\xi) = 1 singles out a preferred direction along the vertical distribution. Left-handed and right-handed chiralities correspond to the two orientations of \xi relative to the complex structure of M. For fermions (fermion), the vertical component \alpha_V transforms with a definite sign under reversal of \xi. Chirality is therefore encoded in the \pm-eigenspaces of the Reeb involution \xi \mapsto -\xi. Bosons (boson), being purely horizontal, are chirality-blind. This is consistent with the observed parity invariance of the electromagnetic and strong interactions. Cf. [nicolaescu2005, petit-2005].
rem:light-cone-affine: Remark Light cone of an affine chart. Consider an open subset U \subset M_0 representing a portion of the descended universe between two regime boundaries. An affine chart on U is a local coordinate patch in which the metric on the base manifold M_0 defines a causal structure. The light cone of the affine chart forms the boundary of the causal future in U. The metric on M_0 determines this light cone, which ensures no singularity of the ambient space is visible from within the chart. In this way, the affine chart provides a non-singular window onto a portion of the Descartes universe.
rem:chirality-trefoil: Remark Chirality and trefoil subgroups. The chirality of the observable universe—manifest in the three colour charges of quantum chromodynamics—is encoded in the symmetry group of the descended surface M_0. genus-maximal descent identifies M_0 as a genus-4 Riemann surface. The construction requires a genus-4 surface whose automorphism group contains three subgroups isomorphic to S_3. These are quotients of the trefoil knot group \pi_1(S^3 \setminus K) \cong \langle x, y \mid x^2 = y^3 \rangle, and they correspond to the three colour charges (red, green, blue). These S_3 subgroups generate a subgroup of the monodromy group. The remaining generators of the full automorphism group act by conjugation, permuting the three S_3 subgroups among themselves.
cor:descartes-braid-structure:
Corollary Braid-group structure of a Descartes universe. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a Descartes universe (Descartes condition). Then:

  1. The braiding of \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) induces a faithful representation \rho_3\colon B_3 \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes 3}) on the fundamental representation V (braid action on tensor products).
  2. The image of \rho_3 in \mathrm{SU}(2) (via the fibre functor \tau) is the binary dihedral group \mathrm{Dic}_3 of order 12 (SU(2) generators).
  3. The composite B_3 \xrightarrow{\rho_3} \mathrm{Dic}_3 \twoheadrightarrow S_3 recovers the three copies of S_3 inside S_5 = \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) (chirality and trefoil), mapping one to each colour sector.
prf:descartes-braid-structure:
Proof Proof of Braid-group structure of a Descartes universe. Item (1) follows from braid action on tensor products applied to the fundamental representation V of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), which is 2-dimensional. The braiding c_{V,V} is computed by the R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) (R-matrix braiding), and faithfulness follows from the fact that the eigenvalues of c_{V,V} are q and -q^{-1}, which are distinct for q \neq \pm 1.

For item (2), the fibre functor \tau sends the braiding to the matrix \check{R} = P \circ \mathcal{R} acting on \mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2. The generators \sigma_1, \sigma_2 map to the \mathrm{SU}(2) elements \alpha, \beta (SU(2) generators) generating \mathrm{Dic}_3, as verified in trefoil operator algebra.

Item (3): the projection \mathrm{Dic}_3 \to S_3 sends \alpha \mapsto (123) and \beta \mapsto (12). The three copies of S_3 inside S_5 are the stabilisers of the three pairs of color coordinates (color sector coords), and conjugation by elements of S_5 \setminus S_3 permutes these copies.

Item (4): the braided monoidal structure of \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) is defined over R[q, q^{-1}] with 30 \in R^{\times} (Bring's surface is QOU(1)), and braid action on tensor products requires no topological input beyond the hexagon axioms.
rem:descartes-braid-structure-generality: Remark Base-ring generality and the \mathfrak{p}-adic realisation. The braid-group structure of a Descartes universe holds over any base ring R with 30 \in R^{\times}. It applies directly to the \mathfrak{p}-adic realisation (p-adic realisation), where knot complements and skein relations remain unavailable.
cor:descartes-knot-eigenbasis: Corollary Knot eigenbasis completeness for a Descartes universe. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a Descartes universe (Descartes condition) with \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) and V the fundamental representation. The knot-type eigenbasis of the algebraic direct limit V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} is complete.
rem:descartes-knot-eigenbasis-derivation:
Remark Derivation of knot-eigenbasis completeness. Completeness of the knot-type eigenbasis follows in four steps.

  1. (Iwahori--Hecke algebra instantiation.) The Descartes condition sets the genus g(M_0) = 4; the volume axiom, independently, sets the gauge group to \mathrm{SU}_q(2), of rank 1 and with two-dimensional fundamental object. The R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) (R-matrix braiding) supplies a braiding c_{V,V} on \mathbf{C} with eigenvalues q and -q^{-1}. The quotient by the quadratic relation (c_{V,V} - q)(c_{V,V} + q^{-1}) = 0 yields the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) acting on V^{\otimes n}.
  2. (Schur--Weyl decomposition.) The Descartes condition demands q not be a root of unity (via 6 \in R^{\times} and non-degeneracy of the Frobenius form). Consequently, H_n(q) is semisimple (Jimbo's theorem). The q-Schur--Weyl decomposition (knot eigenbasis completeness(1)) applies: every V^{\otimes n} decomposes into irreducible summands labelled by two-part partitions \lambda \vdash n.
  3. (Braid representation.) The faithful representation \rho_3 \colon B_3 \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes 3}) (braid-group structure(1)) extends to \rho_n \colon B_n \to \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(V^{\otimes n}) for all n via braid action on tensor products. The Markov trace on the Iwahori--Hecke algebra tower detects every irreducible summand.
  4. (Completeness.) By the combining theorem (knot eigenbasis completeness), the three inputs—Schur--Weyl decomposition, Alexander surjectivity, and Markov trace detection—yield a complete knot-type eigenbasis for the algebraic direct limit V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n}. A finite categorical trace over knot-labelled summands replaces the Feynman path integral.
rem:brings-curve:
Remark Bring's curve is the unique Riemann surface of genus 4 with the maximal automorphism group S_5 (order 120) for its genus. It is defined by the intersection of three symmetric hypersurfaces in \mathbb{P}^4:

  \sum_{j=0}^{4} x_j = 0,
  \qquad
  \sum_{j=0}^{4} x_j^2 = 0,
  \qquad
  \sum_{j=0}^{4} x_j^3 = 0.

The symmetric group S_5 acts by permuting the five homogeneous coordinates. This action realises the monodromy structure described in chirality and trefoil. The group S_5 contains three copies of S_3 (quotients of the trefoil knot group) corresponding to the three colour charges. Elements outside these subgroups act by conjugation, permuting the three copies among themselves.
rem:brings-q-hyperbolic-geometry:
Remark q-Hyperbolic Geometry on Bring's Curve. The classical hyperbolic geometry of Bring's curve (genus g=4) admits a canonical q-deformation governed by the quantum hyperbolic plane \mathrm{SU}_q(1,1).

While the Euclidean sector (E_q(2)) of the theory is governed by the Hahn–Exton q-Bessel function (the third kind, J_\nu^{(3)}(x;q)) as seen in the ladder coefficients, the q-hyperbolic geometry on the Bring's surface fibre is intrinsically described by Jackson's q-Bessel functions of the first and second kinds (J_\nu^{(1)}(x;q) and J_\nu^{(2)}(x;q)). These functions appear as matrix elements of the representations of \mathrm{SU}_q(1,1) and encode the "radial" components of the deformed hyperbolic structures.

The first-order contiguity recurrences satisfied by these coefficients (First-order contiguity recurrence for the Jackson first- and second-kind q-Bessel coefficients (fibre-level)) supply the natural orthogonal basis for the q-hyperbolic deformation of Bring's curve. Their q-weights are adapted to the \mathrm{SU}_q(1,1) Casimir invariants, unlike the third kind's q^{k(k-1)/2} weight.
sec:archimedean-condition-genus-preamble: A two-strand torus knot T(2, 2k+1) has Seifert genus g(T(2, 2k+1)) = k. Because an embedded incompressible Seifert surface on \Sigma_4 cannot have genus exceeding g(\Sigma_4) = 4, the two-strand torus-knot tower truncates sharply at k \leq 4, admitting only the unknot 0_1 (g=0), the trefoil 3_1 (g=1), the cinquefoil 5_1 (g=2), the septafoil 7_1 (g=3), and the nonafoil 9_1 (g=4). This section proves that the Chebyshev degree of the Hecke evaluation polynomials matches the Seifert genus and establishes the rank of the embeddable generator set.
prop:torus-knot-generators:
Proposition Finiteness of the T_{m,n} generator set. The genus g(M_0) = 4 of the base curve forces torus knots to serve as the generators of the particle spectrum. Because Bring's surface has genus g = 4, any T_{m,n} whose Seifert genus exceeds 4 cannot embed. This constraint selects a finite, enumerable generator set \mathcal{G} whose cardinality is entirely determined by g (equivalently by \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = 2 - 2g).

Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a Descartes universe, so that g(M_0) = 4 (Descartes condition). The torus knot T_{m,n} with \gcd(m,n) = 1 and m < n embeds into the Seifert genus-g surface only if:

  g(T_{m,n}) =  \frac{(m-1)(n-1)}{2}  \leq  g(A) =  4.

The constraint (m-1)(n-1) \leq 8 admits exactly six coprime pairs with m \geq 2. Together with the unknot T_{1,0} = 0_1, the generator set has |\mathcal{G}| = 7.

def:photon:
Definition Photon (four-term Hecke element with chiral vertex). Let R be a commutative ring and let H_3(R,q) be the Iwahori--Hecke algebra with generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1. The photon with colour weights (\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) \in R^3 is the four-term element

  \gamma(\varphi) \;=\; \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\,\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\,\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} \;\in\; H_3(R,q).

A photon has three parameters and four terms. Its fourth term is the chiral pair-production vertex V = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}, the \gamma\bar\gamma vertex: one positive crossing on the strands (0,1) and one negative crossing on the strands (1,2). The weight \varphi_{01} is the vertex weight. With h = q - q^{-1} the Hecke relation gives \sigma_1^{-1} = \sigma_1 - h\mathbf{1}, so V = L_+ - h\sigma_0 with L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1, and

  \gamma(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) \;=\; \mathbf{1} + (\varphi_0 - h\varphi_{01})\,\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\,\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\,L_+ .

In the normal-form basis of H_3(R,q) the support of a photon is therefore contained in \{\mathbf{1}, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+\}.

The bare photon is \gamma(0,0,0) = \mathbf{1}, the empty knot. It is the identity element, not the unknot 0_1, which is a closed strand and denotes the neutrino (notation).

Three consequences of the definition fix how the word is used elsewhere:

  1. A single crossing \sigma_i is not a photon. It is the \sigma_i-term of a photon's support.
  2. The form \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 is the specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0, not a second definition.
  3. L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 and e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 are not in the normal-form support of one photon.
prop:photon-augmentation-jet:
Proposition The augmentation jet of H_n(q) vanishes, and a photon is not augmentation-normalised. Let R be a commutative ring, q \in R a unit, h = q - q^{-1} and [2]_q = q + q^{-1}. If \sigma in an R-algebra satisfies \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1, then

  (\sigma - q)^2 = -[2]_q\,(\sigma - q).

Let \varepsilon : H_n(q) \to R be the augmentation \varepsilon(\sigma_i) = q and I = \ker\varepsilon. If R is a field and [2]_q \neq 0, then I = I^2, so I/I^2 = 0. The same holds for the sign augmentation \varepsilon(\sigma_i) = -q^{-1}. For every photon,

  \varepsilon\bigl(\gamma(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01})\bigr) = 1 + q\,(\varphi_0 + \varphi_1) + \varphi_{01},

so \gamma(\varphi) - 1 \in I only on the hyperplane q(\varphi_0 + \varphi_1) + \varphi_{01} = 0.

Proof. Expand (\sigma - q)^2 = \sigma^2 - 2q\sigma + q^2 and substitute \sigma^2 = h\sigma + 1; the result is -(q + q^{-1})\sigma + q^2 + 1 = -[2]_q(\sigma - q). The ideal I is generated by the elements \sigma_i - q. When [2]_q is invertible, each generator equals -[2]_q^{-1}(\sigma_i - q)^2 \in I^2, and I^2 is a two-sided ideal, so I \subseteq I^2. For the photon, \varepsilon(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}) = q \cdot q^{-1} = 1. \square
prop:photon-response-determines-q:
Proposition The one-photon Markov-trace response determines q under convention D. Let K be a field, q \in K with q \neq 0 and q^2 + 1 \neq 0, h = q - q^{-1}, and let \mathrm{tr}_M be the Markov trace on H_3(q) with parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). For every photon,

  \mathrm{tr}_M\,\gamma(\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) = 1 + z\,(\varphi_0 + \varphi_1) + z\,(z - h)\,\varphi_{01}.

If p \in K with p \neq 0, p^2 + 1 \neq 0 gives the same function of (\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}), then p = q or q^4 + 1 = 0.

Proof. The Markov rules give \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z, and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}) = \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\sigma_0(\sigma_1 - h)\bigr) = z^2 - hz. Equal functions have equal coefficients, so p and q give the same z and the same z(z - h), hence the same h. From q - q^{-1} = p - p^{-1} follows (q - p)(qp + 1) = 0. If p = -q^{-1}, equality of q^3/(q^2+1) and p^3/(p^2+1) reduces to (q^4 + 1)(q^2 + 1) = 0. \square
conj:bring-isospectrality-question:
Conjecture Open question: is Bring's surface spectrally rigid?. Open question. Is Bring's surface \mathcal{B}, with its hyperbolic metric, Laplace-isospectral to a hyperbolic surface that is not isometric to it? The same question can be asked of the quantum observable universe built on \mathcal{B}, with the spectrum of the categorical Dirac operator in place of the Laplacian. No answer is conjectured here.

Kac asked whether the spectrum of a domain determines its shape [kac1966], and Sunada gave a general construction of isospectral non-isometric manifolds [sunada1985]: a finite group G acting on a manifold X, with two subgroups H_1, H_2 \le G that meet every conjugacy class of G in the same number of elements but are not conjugate, gives isospectral quotients X/H_1 and X/H_2. Three facts bear on the question for \mathcal{B}.

  1. Sunada pairs inside the automorphism group. Neither \mathrm{Aut}^+(\mathcal{B}) \cong S_5 nor the full group S_5 \times C_2 contains such a pair of subgroups. A Sunada partner of \mathcal{B} would therefore need a group acting on a proper cover X of \mathcal{B}, with \mathcal{B} = X/H_1.
  2. The trace parameter is determined. Under the Markov trace of convention D, the one-photon response determines q (one-photon response).
  3. States are determined up to the radical of the trace form. The zero-photon response \mathrm{tr}_M(x) factors through the cocenter H_n(q)/[H_n(q), H_n(q)]. The k-photon responses \mathrm{tr}_M(\gamma(\varphi^1)\cdots\gamma(\varphi^k)\,x) determine much more. Products of photons span H_n(q) (stopping depth), so these responses determine x modulo the radical \{u : \mathrm{tr}_M(yu) = 0 \text{ for all } y\} of the trace form. Under convention D on H_3(q), that radical is the line spanned by the sign idempotent: a state is heard except for its alternating component.

The question would be settled by a group G acting on a cover of \mathcal{B} with a pair H_1, H_2 as above and X/H_1 \cong \mathcal{B}, X/H_2 \not\cong \mathcal{B}, or by a proof that the spectrum of \mathcal{B} determines it. The eigenvalues of surfaces with large symmetry groups are studied in [cook2021].
prop:bring-harmonic-types:
Proposition The harmonics of Bring's surface by S5 type, exhaustively. Let \mathcal{B} be Bring's surface with \mathrm{Aut}^+(\mathcal{B}) \cong S_5, presented by the Bring map. Let E be any finite-dimensional S_5-module of functions or forms on \mathcal{B}, for instance an eigenspace E_\lambda of the Laplacian.

  1. (Exhaustiveness.) The character of E is \sum_\rho m_\rho\,\chi_\rho for unique integers m_\rho \ge 0, where \rho runs over the seven types [5], [1^5], [4,1], [2,1^3], [3,2], [2^2,1], [3,1^2]. There is no other type.
  2. (Quotients.) For H \le S_5, the H-invariant part of E has dimension d_H = \sum_\rho \dim\rho^H\, m_\rho, and the 19 \times 7 table \dim \rho^H satisfies \sum_\rho \dim\rho \cdot \dim\rho^H = [S_5 : H]. The column of [2,1^3] = \mathrm{std}\otimes\mathrm{sgn} is the genus of \mathcal{B}/H, so a quotient that is a sphere sees no harmonic of that type.
  3. (Recovery.) For H = S_3,\ S_3 \times S_2,\ A_4,\ F_{20},\ S_4,\ A_5,\ S_5 the 7 \times 7 block is unimodular, and
\begin{aligned}
m_{[5]} &= d_{S_5}, & m_{[1^5]} &= d_{A_5} - d_{S_5}, & m_{[4,1]} &= d_{S_4} - d_{S_5}, \\
m_{[3,2]} &= d_{S_3\times S_2} - d_{S_4}, & m_{[2^2,1]} &= d_{F_{20}} - d_{S_5}, & m_{[2,1^3]} &= d_{A_4} - d_{S_4} - d_{A_5} + d_{S_5}, \\
m_{[3,1^2]} &= d_{S_3} - d_{S_3\times S_2} - d_{S_4} + d_{S_5}. &&&&
\end{aligned}

So the typed Laplace spectrum of \mathcal{B} is determined by the untyped spectra of six sphere orbifolds and one torus orbifold \mathcal{B}/A_4. The 19 rows are pairwise distinct, so S_5 contains no Sunada pair (item 1 of the isospectrality question). 4. (One quotient suffices up to translation.) Every type has a vector fixed by \langle(01)(23)\rangle and by C_3, so every harmonic of \mathcal{B} is a sum of S_5-translates of lifts from the genus-2 quotient \mathcal{B}/\langle(01)(23)\rangle. No sphere or torus quotient has this property. 5. (Cellular harmonics.) The harmonic 1-cochains of the Bring map form 2\cdot[2,1^3], and its vertex functions form [5] + [4,1] + [2,1^3] + [3,2] + 2\,[2^2,1] + [3,1^2].
prf:bring-harmonic-types: Proof Proof of the classification of the harmonics of Bring's surface by S5 type. Item 1: the seven characters satisfy both the row and the column orthogonality relations, so they form a basis of the class functions on the seven classes of S_5, and \sum_\rho (\dim\rho)^2 = 120. A class function f is therefore \sum_\rho \langle f, \chi_\rho\rangle \chi_\rho, uniquely; by Maschke the character of E determines E. Item 2 is \dim \rho^H = |H|^{-1}\sum_{h\in H}\chi_\rho(h), evaluated on the class distribution of each of the 19 subgroup classes, and Frobenius reciprocity for \mathrm{Ind}_H^{S_5} 1. The [2,1^3] column agrees with the genus table of the quotients because H^0(\mathcal{B}, K) \cong [2,1^3] and g(\mathcal{B}/H) = \dim H^0(K)^H. Item 3: the block times the displayed integer matrix is the identity, so its determinant is \pm 1. Item 4 reads off two rows with no zero entry. Item 5: the cells of the map are the cosets of \langle S\rangle \cong C_4, \langle A\rangle \cong C_2 and \langle SA\rangle \cong C_5, and the edge stabiliser reverses its edge, so the cochain characters are \mathrm{Ind}\,1, \mathrm{Ind}\,\mathrm{sgn} and \mathrm{Ind}\,1. The Hopf trace formula with H^0 = H^2 = [5] gives \chi_{H^1} = 2[5] - (\chi_{C^0} - \chi_{C^1} + \chi_{C^2}) = 2\,\chi_{[2,1^3]}. Every step is integer arithmetic checked in Lean. \square
prop:hopf-trace-formula:
Proposition Hopf trace formula for a two-step complex. Proposition. Let K be a field and C_2 \xrightarrow{d_2} C_1 \xrightarrow{d_1} C_0 finite-dimensional K-vector spaces with d_1 d_2 = 0. Let (f_0, f_1, f_2) be a chain map, d_1 f_1 = f_0 d_1 and d_2 f_2 = f_1 d_2. With H_0 = C_0/\operatorname{im} d_1, H_1 = \ker d_1/\operatorname{im} d_2 and H_2 = \ker d_2,

\operatorname{tr} f_0 - \operatorname{tr} f_1 + \operatorname{tr} f_2 = \operatorname{tr}(f \mid H_0) - \operatorname{tr}(f \mid H_1) + \operatorname{tr}(f \mid H_2).

If C_k = K^{X_k} for a finite set X_k of cells and f_k permutes the cells, \operatorname{tr} f_k is the number of fixed cells.

Proof. For an endomorphism f of V preserving a subspace W, \operatorname{tr} f = \operatorname{tr}(f|_W) + \operatorname{tr}(f \text{ on } V/W). To see this, choose a linear section s of \pi : V \to V/W and put r = \mathrm{id} - s\pi, a map into W, so \iota r + s\pi = \mathrm{id}; then cyclicity of trace gives \operatorname{tr} f = \operatorname{tr}(r f \iota) + \operatorname{tr}(\pi f s). Apply this to \operatorname{im} d_1 \subseteq C_0, \ker d_1 \subseteq C_1, \operatorname{im} d_2 \subseteq \ker d_1 and \ker d_2 \subseteq C_2. The isomorphisms C_1/\ker d_1 \cong \operatorname{im} d_1 and C_2/\ker d_2 \cong \operatorname{im} d_2 intertwine the induced maps, so the two middle terms cancel in pairs. For a permuted basis, the diagonal entry at a cell is 1 when the cell is fixed and 0 otherwise. \square

Use. This is the formula behind hopf_trace_h1 in prop:bring-harmonic-types, where \chi_{C_k}(g) counts the cells of Bring's map fixed by g. What stays cited there is that the cellular homology of the map is the homology of the surface, with H_0 trivial and H_2 the orientation character, and the Hodge splitting of H^1.
prop:quaternion-conjugation-orientation:
Proposition Quaternion conjugation, orientation and the cone chirality. Proposition. On the cone \mathbb{H}_R = Quaternion R, over any commutative ring R, let \Gamma_i(p) = i\,p\,i be the chirality grading.

  1. Conjugation p \mapsto \bar p satisfies \overline{qp} = \bar p\,\bar q, so it turns left multiplication by q into right multiplication by \bar q, and it exchanges the two \mathrm{SU}(2) factors of \mathrm{Spin}(4).
  2. In coordinates conjugation is \mathrm{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1), of determinant -1, while left multiplication by q has determinant (\mathrm{N}q)^2. So conjugation reverses orientation, and a unit quaternion preserves it.
  3. Conjugation keeps \Gamma_i: \overline{\Gamma_i(\bar p)} = \Gamma_i(p). For a general pure u it sends \Gamma_u(p) = u\,p\,i to p \mapsto i\,p\,u.
  4. If w is a unit with wi = -iw, then p \mapsto w\,\overline{\Gamma_i(\overline{\bar w p})} equals -\Gamma_i(p). So L_w \circ \bar{\ } reverses orientation and flips the chirality grading at once.

Proof. (1) and (3) are \overline{ab} = \bar b \bar a with \bar i = -i. (2) is a determinant expansion. (4) uses i\bar w = -\bar w i, which follows from wi = -iw and w\bar w = \bar w w = 1. \square

Reading. By prop:hypercharge-sign-is-bring-orientation, the hypercharge sign is the orientation bit of Bring's surface. On the cone, conjugation reverses orientation but keeps \Gamma_i. A perpendicular unit w, for example in 2I, flips \Gamma_i but keeps orientation. Only L_w \circ \bar{\ } does both. So the cone's chirality equals the hypercharge sign exactly when Bring's reflection acts on the cone as L_w \circ \bar{\ } rather than as conjugation alone. The corpus does not yet construct the S_5 \times C_2 action on the cone, so this is open. As with the complex volume (prop:complex-volume-sign-placement), the quaternions place the bit but do not fix it.
prop:bring-reflection-parity:
Proposition Reflection parity of the harmonics of Bring's surface. On the darts S_5 of the Bring map, let T = (2\,4), the unique element with TST = S^{-1}, TAT = A and T^2 = 1. Then c(x) = xT is an orientation-reversing automorphism of the map that commutes with S_5, and the full isometry group is S_5 \times \langle c \rangle, of order 240.

  1. c fixes no vertex, edge or face, so it acts freely. \mathcal{B}/c is a closed non-orientable surface with \chi = -3. This matches the curve: c is complex conjugation, and \sum x_i^2 = 0 has no nonzero real solution.
  2. The sides of the (2,4,5) flag triangle are the mirrors of (T, c), (ST, c) and (AT, c). Their pairwise products are S^{-1}, A and SA, and T is odd while ST and AT are even. So the four one-dimensional types are boundary problems on the triangle: [5]^+ is Neumann on every side, [5]^- is Dirichlet on every side, [1^5]^+ is Dirichlet on the edge side and Neumann on the other two, and [1^5]^- is the reverse.
  3. Every type of the classification by S_5 type splits as \rho^+ \oplus \rho^-, and the fourteen types of S_5 \times C_2 are exhaustive. The harmonic 1-cochains are [2,1^3]^+ \oplus [2,1^3]^-. The vertex functions are [5]^+ + [4,1]^+ + [2,1^3]^- + [3,2]^+ + [2^2,1]^+ + [2^2,1]^- + [3,1^2]^-.
  4. For any eigenspace of the Laplacian, the fourteen multiplicities m_\rho^\pm are integer combinations of its multiplicities on the seven quotients \mathcal{B}/H of the classification and on the seven quotients \mathcal{B}/(H \times \langle c \rangle).
prf:bring-reflection-parity: Proof Proof of the reflection parity of the harmonics of Bring's surface. The relations for T, and its uniqueness, are checked over all of S_5. The isometry (g, c)\colon x \mapsto gxT fixes the vertex x\langle S\rangle if and only if x^{-1}gxT \in \langle S \rangle. It keeps the edge \{x, xA\} with its direction if and only if gxT = x, and reverses it if and only if gxT = xA. It fixes the face through x if and only if x^{-1}gxTA \in \langle AS\rangle. Counting over the 120 darts gives fixed cells only for g a transposition (6 vertices, 6 edges kept) and for g a double transposition (4 vertices, 4 edges reversed, 8 faces). For g = 1 there are none. A kept face has its orientation reversed. With H^0 = [5]^+ and H^2 = [5]^-, the Hopf trace formula gives \operatorname{tr}((g,c) \mid H^1) = 1 - 1 - (C^0 - C^1 + C^2) = 0 for every g, so H^1 is [2,1^3]^+ \oplus [2,1^3]^-. Since c is central, a class function on S_5 \times C_2 is a pair (f_0, f_1), and m_\rho^\pm = \langle f_0 \pm f_1, \chi_\rho\rangle/240. For item 4, (\rho\otimes\varepsilon)^{H\times\langle c\rangle} is \rho^H when \varepsilon = + and 0 when \varepsilon = -, so the recovery matrix of the classification applies to each parity. \square
prop:bring-spectral-sunset-selection:
Proposition Selection rule for the typed spectral sunset on Bring's surface. Let G = \sum_{\lambda \ne 0} \varphi_\lambda \otimes \varphi_\lambda / \lambda be the Green function of the Laplacian on \mathcal{B}, with a real orthonormal eigenbasis adapted to the fourteen types \rho^\pm of the reflection parity. The two-loop sunset is

  \iint G(x,y)^3 \, dx\, dy = \sum_{a,b,c} w_a w_b w_c\, C_{abc}^2, \qquad w = 1/\lambda, \qquad C_{abc} = \int \varphi_a \varphi_b \varphi_c .

Let N(\rho,\sigma,\tau) = \dim \mathrm{Hom}_{S_5}(\rho\otimes\sigma\otimes\tau, 1). Then C_{abc} = 0 unless N(\rho_a,\rho_b,\rho_c) \ne 0 and an even number of a, b, c are reflection-odd. On every energy-bounded cut of the spectrum, the sunset is therefore a sum of partial sunsets over the 572 allowed typed triples out of 14^3 = 2744. At the S_5 level, 143 of the 343 ordered triples of types are allowed, and 0 \le N \le 2. In particular N([2,1^3],[2,1^3],[2,1^3]) = 0, so three modes of the holomorphic type never couple.
prf:bring-spectral-sunset-selection: Proof Proof of the selection rule for the typed spectral sunset. N(\rho,\sigma,\tau) = \langle \chi_\rho\chi_\sigma\chi_\tau, 1\rangle, because the characters of S_5 are real. It is computed exactly from the character table, and the counts 200 forbidden and 143 allowed are checked by enumeration. The integral is invariant under S_5 \times \langle c\rangle, so (u,v,w) \mapsto \int uvw is an invariant trilinear form. On \rho_a \otimes \rho_b \otimes \rho_c it vanishes when N = 0, by Schur's lemma. Since \varphi \circ c = \pm\varphi, it also vanishes when the product of the three parities is -1. Splitting each of the three sums over the cut by type and parity gives the sum of partial sunsets. Each forbidden partial sunset is zero term by term. \square
prop:bring-discrete-sunset:
Proposition The exact discrete sunset on the Bring map graph. Let \Gamma be the vertex graph of the Bring map \{5,4\}: 30 vertices (the cosets x\langle S\rangle), each of degree 4, with an edge for each of the 60 edges \{x, xA\}. Let \Delta = 4I - \mathrm{Adj} be its graph Laplacian, and G its Green function on mean-zero functions, \Delta G = I - J/30.

(i) Functions on the vertices split under S_5 \times \langle c\rangle as

  \mathbb{Q}^{30} = \mathrm{triv}^+ \oplus \mathrm{std}^+ \oplus [2,1^3]^- \oplus [3,2]^+ \oplus [2,2,1]^+ \oplus [2,2,1]^- \oplus [3,1,1]^-,

each type with multiplicity one, so \Delta is a scalar \lambda on each: \lambda = 0, 5, 7, 2, 6, 4, 2 in that order. Hence \mathrm{spec}\,\Delta = \{0^1, 2^{11}, 4^5, 5^4, 6^5, 7^4\}. The eigenvalue 2 carries two types, [3,2]^+ \oplus [3,1,1]^-.

(ii) Write G = \sum_{k \ne \mathrm{triv}} P_k/\lambda_k with P_k the typed projectors. The typed partial sunset \sum_{x,y} G_a(x,y)\,G_b(x,y)\,G_c(x,y), G_k = P_k/\lambda_k, vanishes on every triple forbidden by the selection rule of the spectral sunset.

(iii) The rule is necessary, not sufficient: \mathrm{std}^+ \otimes \mathrm{std}^+ \otimes [3,2]^+ is allowed (N = 1, all even), and its partial sunset is 0. The other 25 unordered allowed triples of nontrivial types are nonzero.

(iv) The discrete sunset is

  \sum_{x,y \in \Gamma} G(x,y)^3 = \frac{18364201}{22680000}.
prf:bring-discrete-sunset: Proof Proof of the exact discrete sunset on the Bring map graph. Everything is a finite computation over \mathbb{Z}, checked in Lean by kernel evaluation. The 30 vertex representatives lie in distinct cosets of \langle S\rangle, which therefore exhaust S_5. The neighbour table and the action tables of S, A (which generate S_5), of the class representatives, and of the reflection x \mapsto xT are checked against the map, coset by coset. The seven integer matrices 120 P_k sum to 120 I. They satisfy P_k P_l = \delta_{kl} P_k and commute with S, A and c. On the image of P_k, the trace of g and of gc is \chi_{\rho_k}(g) and \pm\chi_{\rho_k}(g) on every class, so that image is \rho_k^\pm. Each P_k satisfies \Delta P_k = \lambda_k P_k, and the traces give the multiplicities. With 50400\,G = \sum_k (420/\lambda_k)\, 120 P_k, the identity \Delta G = I - J/30 is checked directly. For each of the 7^3 ordered typed triples, \sum_{x,y}(120P_a)(120P_b)(120P_c) is evaluated: it is 0 whenever the triple is forbidden, and it is 0 for (\mathrm{std}^+, \mathrm{std}^+, [3,2]^+). Finally \sum_{x,y}(50400\,G)^3 = 103662241804800, and dividing by 50400^3 gives (iv). \square
prop:bring-orbifold-signatures:
Proposition Orbifold signatures of the symmetry quotients of Bring's surface. Let H run over the 19 conjugacy classes of subgroups of S_5, and let c be the central reflection of the reflection parity.

(i) The quotient \mathcal{B}/H is a closed orientable orbifold whose cone points are determined by the class distribution of H. If k_{(2)}, k_{(22)}, k_{(4)}, k_{(5)} count the transpositions, double transpositions, 4-cycles and 5-cycles of H, it has

  \frac{4k_{(22)} - 2k_{(4)} + 12k_{(2)}}{|H|} \text{ cone points of order } 2, \qquad \frac{4k_{(4)}}{|H|} \text{ of order } 4, \qquad \frac{5k_{(5)}}{|H|} \text{ of order } 5 .

So \mathcal{B}/S_5 = (0;2,4,5), \mathcal{B}/A_5 = (0;2,5,5), \mathcal{B}/S_4 = (0;2,2,2,4), \mathcal{B}/F_{20} = (0;4,4,5), \mathcal{B}/A_4 = (1;2), \mathcal{B}/(S_3\times S_2) = (0;2^5) and \mathcal{B}/S_3 = (0;2^6).

(ii) The quotient \mathcal{B}/(H\times\langle c\rangle) has a mirror if and only if H contains a transposition or a double transposition, and then its boundary is one curve. For the seven recovery subgroups it is a disc with corner reflectors 2,4,5 (S_5), a disc with corners 2,5,5 (A_5), a disc with one cone point 2 and corners 2,4 (S_4), a disc with cone 4 and corner 5 (F_{20}), a Möbius band with one corner 2 (A_4), a disc with cone 2 and corners 2,2,2 (S_3 \times S_2), and a disc with cones 2,2,2 (S_3).

(iii) Every one of the 38 quotients satisfies the orbifold Euler characteristic formula \chi(X) - \sum(1 - 1/m) - \tfrac12\sum(1 - 1/n) = \chi(\mathcal{B})/|K| = -6/|K|.
prf:bring-orbifold-signatures: Proof Proof of the orbifold signatures of the symmetry quotients. On the map, S_5 acts freely on darts, so every cell stabiliser is cyclic. At a vertex it is a conjugate of \langle S\rangle \cong C_4; at an edge it is generated by a conjugate of the transposition A, which reverses the edge; at a face it is a conjugate of \langle AS\rangle \cong C_5. Let n_d count the cells whose H-stabiliser has order exactly d. These cells fall into d\,n_d/|H| orbits, each a cone point of order d. By Burnside, n_d is a sum of fixed-cell counts over elements of H. A 4-cycle fixes 2 vertices and each C_4 has two generators, so n_4 = k_{(4)}. A double transposition fixes 2 vertices and each C_4 contains one, so n_2^V = 2k_{(22)} - k_{(4)}. A transposition fixes 6 edges, so n_2^E = 6k_{(2)}. A 5-cycle fixes 4 faces and each C_5 has four generators, so n_5 = k_{(5)}. This gives (i). The genera agree with the harmonic types, and the Euler characteristic check is integer arithmetic. For (ii), (g,c) fixes a point only when g is a transposition or a double transposition. The quotient complexes of the barycentric (2,4,5) triangulation, on which S_5\times C_2 acts simply transitively on the 240 triangles, give the table: orbits of cells, stabilisers, mirror edges, and a 2-colouring for orientability. Lean checks this table against (iii), against the mirror criterion, and against the classification of compact surfaces. \square
prop:photon-filtration-depth-bounds:
Proposition Bounds on the photon stopping depth L(n). Let n \ge 2, N = n(n-1)/2, and let F_1 \subset H_n(q) be spanned by 1 and the sliding photons' terms \sigma_i (0 \le i \le n-2) and \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1} (0 \le i \le n-3). Let F_k be the span of products of at most k elements of F_1, and L(n) the least k with F_k = H_n(q). Then

  \left\lceil \tfrac{N}{2} \right\rceil \;\le\; L(n) \;\le\; \left\lfloor \tfrac{n^2}{4} \right\rfloor .

Proof. Let C_m be the span of the Iwahori–Matsumoto basis elements T_w with \ell(w) \le m. Then C_aC_b \subseteq C_{a+b}, and T_{w_0} \notin C_{N-1} [iwahori1964]. Since \sigma_i = T_{s_i} and \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1} = T_{s_is_{i+1}} - (q - q^{-1})\,T_{s_i}, we have F_1 \subseteq C_2. Hence F_k \subseteq C_{2k}, and T_{w_0} \in F_k forces N \le 2k.

For the upper bound, write every w as a reduced product of increasing runs s_a s_{a+1} \cdots s_b of lengths r_j \le j, j = 1, \dots, n-1. This is the inverse of the decreasing-run normal form of w^{-1}. A run of length r equals a product of \lfloor r/2 \rfloor elements \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1} and at most one \sigma_i, up to terms of smaller length. So F_K contains T_w + (\text{shorter terms}) for every w, with K = \sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\lceil j/2\rceil = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor. These n! elements are unitriangular in the basis \{T_w\}, so they span H_n(q). \square
conj:photon-stopping-depth:
Conjecture The photon stopping depth is \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor. For every n \ge 2, the photon stopping depth of the bounds proposition attains its upper bound: L(n) = \lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor.

The upper bound is attained for n = 3, 4, 5, 6, where L(n) = 2, 4, 6, 9. The lower bound \lceil n(n-1)/4 \rceil is not attained for any n between 4 and 6. A proof would need a lower bound sharper than the one from Coxeter length.
prop:borromean-photon-factorisations:
Proposition Linking neutrality selects the photon factorisation of the Borromean core. Let h = q - q^{-1} with h \ne 0 and h^2 + 2 \ne 0, over a domain. Suppose two photons satisfy \gamma(\varphi)\,\gamma(\psi) = V^3 with V = \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1}. Suppose also that, in the formal expansion of \gamma(\varphi)\gamma(\psi) in the group algebra of B_3, the coefficients of the four braid elements \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0V, \sigma_1V vanish:

  \varphi_0 + \psi_0 + \varphi_{01}\psi_1 = 0,\quad \varphi_1 + \psi_1 = 0,\quad \varphi_0\psi_{01} = 0,\quad \varphi_1\psi_{01} = 0 .

Then \varphi_0 = \varphi_1 = \psi_0 = \psi_1 = 0, and \{\varphi_{01}, \psi_{01}\} = \{qh, -q^{-1}h\}, so the factorisation is the one in the two-photon factorisation.

Proof. Write the six coordinate equations of \gamma(\varphi)\gamma(\psi) = V^3 in the basis T_e, T_0, T_1, T_{01}, T_{10}, T_{010}. If \psi_{01} = 0, a combination of these equations with the four conditions gives h^3(h^2 + 2) = 0, which is excluded. Otherwise the last two conditions give \varphi_0 = \varphi_1 = 0, and then \psi_1 = 0 and \psi_0 = 0. Both photons then lie on the line 1 + R\,V. Because 1, V, V^2 are linearly independent and V^3 = 1 + h^2V - h^2V^2, the vertex weights satisfy \varphi_{01} + \psi_{01} = h^2 and \varphi_{01}\psi_{01} = -h^2. \square

The four braid elements above are not linking-neutral, while 1, V and V^2 are. The expansion contains five further non-neutral elements, \sigma_0^2, \sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, \sigma_1^2 and V\sigma_0. Imposing linking neutrality on each term of the expansion sets all nine coefficients to zero, and the four used above already force the conclusion. Under that reading of neutrality the vertex weights qh and -q^{-1}h are derived rather than chosen.
prop:cohomological-embedding:
Proposition Cohomological embedding: torus knot representations exhaust H^1(\Sigma_g). The torus knots embeddable on the moduli surface \Sigma_g form a complete set of representations, exhausting the available cohomology and spanning the space of knot observables.

(i) Embeddability = representation. A torus knot T_{r,s} with \gcd(r, s) = 1 admits a representation in \mathbf{C} if and only if its Seifert rank embeds in the first cohomology of \Sigma_g:

  \mathrm{rank} H_1(\mathrm{Seifert}(T_{r,s}))
  =  \frac{(r-1)(s-1)}{2}  \leq  g

(ii) Fiber degree. The maximum fiber degree for T_{r, p^k} on \Sigma_g is:

  k_{\max}(r, p, g)
  = \max\!\left\{k : \frac{(r-1)(p^k - 1)}{2} \leq g\right\}

(iii) Completeness. The Jones polynomials of embeddable torus knots span the space of knot invariants on \Sigma_g.

(iv) Genus 4 is forced. The QOU axioms require T_{2,3} and T_{2,9} to embed, but T_{2,11} must not. This uniquely forces g = 4 and \chi = -6.

See Table 1.

The cohomology of \Sigma_4 admits a knot basis:

  H^*(\Sigma_4)
  = \underbrace{H^0 \oplus H^2}_{\dim 2} \oplus \underbrace{H^{1,0}}_{\dim 4} \oplus \underbrace{H^{0,1}}_{\dim 4}

See Table 2.

The 6 embeddable knots form a complete basis spanning the 5-dimensional space of irrep characters. Every observable hadron is a composite of these 6 blocks, and every interaction is mediated by the 7 associated transfer matrices (including free propagation). Genus 4 is the unique minimal environment that supports \mathrm{SU}_2 reconstruction and strong binding without introducing unobserved spurious matter.

rem:torus-knot-generators-interpretation:
Remark Physical interpretation of the torus-knot generators.

  1. Lepton generations. The electron is the braid word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link; the trefoil T_{2,3} is kept as a backup electron. The torus-knot tower T_{2,3}, T_{2,5}, T_{2,7} at Reeb degrees 1, 2, 3 is the backup lepton family. Within that family only the first two are S_5-equivariant under the \mathbb{Z}_n \hookrightarrow S_5 criterion; the third embeds topologically but breaks its \mathbb{Z}_7 symmetry. T_{2,9} saturates g = 4 (symmetry-broken), and T_{2,11} is genus-excluded, precluding a fourth member.
  2. Quark sector. The (3,n)-family generators T_{3,4} and T_{3,5} act as H^{0,1} force carriers. T_{3,4} encodes Hopf-squared color binding, while T_{3,5} mediates the weak interaction. As a braid, T_{3,5} = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 is the electron word cubed times one letter, (\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0)^3\sigma_1 in B_3, and it is the only member of the family T_{3,3m+2} within the genus bound that reaches g = 4. The three-strand meridional winding resonantly threads the three color tubes.
  3. Saturation. The seventh generator T_{2,9} at genus 4 exactly saturates Bring's surface. New particle types would require composite construction by linking existing knots.
  4. Hyperbolic knots. The figure-eight 4_1 and three-twist 5_2 are not generators. They arise from Skein crossing changes applied to linked torus-knot configurations, inheriting nonzero hyperbolic volume and bare mass from the linking process.

The bound N(\chi) = 1 - \chi = 7 on the number of generators equals the number of handles (g = 4) plus the three independent Seifert genus values available within them. The recursive brane tower does not increase the genus, making the generator count stable across all levels.
thm:embeddability-closure:
Theorem Embeddability closure under knot-particle generation. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the Descartes universe with \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 and fiber genus g(\Sigma_4) = 4. Let K be any knot type appearing as a component of a link produced by a finite sequence of Hopf linkings \ell_H, color-tube threadings \ell_c, and Skein crossing changes \sigma applied to generators in \mathcal{G}. Then:

  1. The Seifert genus of K satisfies 
      g(K) \leq 4.
  2. K admits a localized knot structure (c, K) \in \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, A^{\mathrm{co}T}) \times \mathrm{Knot} at some point c.
  3. The localized knot (c, K) descends under \tau to an observable morphism in \mathbf{C}: every generated particle interacts with every other generated particle via the categorical braiding.

The generation scheme is thus closed under observability.
rem:embeddability-closure-spectral-filte:
Remark Genus behaviour of the generation moves and the genus-4 spectral filter. The embeddability closure rests on how each generation move acts on the Seifert genus, together with a spectral filter at genus 4.

Hopf linking \ell_H and Color-tube threading \ell_c preserve each component's knot type and Seifert genus. The structures live in the total space and do not increase the genus of any individual component.

Skein crossing change \sigma alters the Seifert genus by at most \pm 1:

  |g(L_+) - g(L_-)| \leq 1, \qquad
  g(L_0) \leq \max\{g(L_+), g(L_-)\}.

While a crossing change might produce a knot of genus 5, Bring's surface imposes a spectral filter: only knots with g(K) \leq 4 admit localized knot structures. The physical state space V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} vanishes for g = 5 descendants because the fibre functor \tau cannot evaluate them.

This spectral filter acts directly at the level of the Skein resolution:

  q  [L_+] - q^{-1} [L_-]
  = (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}) [L_0].

Terms with g > 4 lie in the kernel of the mass functional \mathfrak{m}. The physical mass receives contributions only from embeddable terms. Every knot in the standard dictionary has g(K) \leq 4. Skein descendants like 4_1 typically exhibit lower genus than their parent generators.

rem:embeddability-closure-interpretation: Remark Embeddability closure and the absence of dark sectors. Because every knot type produced by generation remains embeddable in the genus-4 fiber, all fundamental particles interact. They all descend to the same base manifold and participate in categorical braiding. A hypothetical genus-5 particle would be unobservable and have zero coupling to other particles. The \chi = -6 constraint thus guarantees a self-consistent, fully interacting particle spectrum with no dark sectors.
